content.text: Review only the current uncommitted diff in analysis/scintillation-dsa-lorentzian-2026-07-07/{run_dsa_lorentzian_fits.py,test_driver_guards.py,README.md}. Do not edit and do not inspect memory. The prior review finding about hard-coded sharedzeta filenames has been fixed by using citable_alpha_roster.json. Return only actionable remaining findings, with severity and file/line anchors, focusing on scientific correctness, multi-component handling, units, uncertainty propagation, provenance, and tests. If none, say no findings.
I’ll review only those three uncommitted diffs and keep this to actionable findings. I won’t edit files or look at memory.
The repo hook requires compact RTK output for `git diff`, so I’m rerunning the same path-limited reads through `rtk`.
The compact diff shows the main risk area is the new PBF overlay and plotting contract. I’m reading the surrounding current code with line numbers now so any findings can be anchored precisely.

- **P1** [run_dsa_lorentzian_fits.py:465](/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS-scint-revalidation/analysis/scintillation-dsa-lorentzian-2026-07-07/run_dsa_lorentzian_fits.py:465) `_load_pbf_fit_for_burst` does not actually enforce the roster gate before loading a PBF fit. It records `_roster_gate_final`, but any entry with a `nickname` and `fit_json` from the included roster buckets will be overlaid, even if its final gate is not usable/citable. The new test name says “excludes_gate_failures”, but it only checks one absent burst name, not a present gate-failed entry. Add an explicit gate/rail-class predicate before returning the payload, and test it with a synthetic or monkeypatched roster containing a matching burst with `fit_json` plus failed/non-citable gate metadata.

- **P1** [run_dsa_lorentzian_fits.py:615](/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS-scint-revalidation/analysis/scintillation-dsa-lorentzian-2026-07-07/run_dsa_lorentzian_fits.py:615) The free `gamma` power-law fit pools every clean Lorentzian component into one bandwidth-frequency relation. For multi-component bursts, component 1 and component 2 can represent different temporal sub-components or scattering scales; fitting them as one population can produce a scientifically misleading `alpha_gamma` and uncertainty band. Split the fit by component identity or only fit a component family that is explicitly adjudicated as comparable across sub-bands; otherwise suppress the single `alpha_gamma` label when multiple clean components per burst are present.

- **P2** [run_dsa_lorentzian_fits.py:670](/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS-scint-revalidation/analysis/scintillation-dsa-lorentzian-2026-07-07/run_dsa_lorentzian_fits.py:670) The PBF overlay uncertainty band samples `tau_1ghz` and `alpha` as independent symmetric Gaussians from averaged upper/lower errors. Joint PBF fits usually have tau-alpha covariance and potentially asymmetric/non-Gaussian posteriors, so this can understate or reshape the predicted bandwidth envelope. Prefer posterior samples/covariance from the fit JSON when available; if only marginal percentiles exist, mark the envelope as approximate in the returned provenance and figure/report text.
